classification.difficultyReason: Development: link the 193% total and permission for multiple selections to overlapping categories that cannot represent parts of one whole. This applies the taught critique of unsuitable graph types.

inlines.text: A poll before an election asked “who would you vote for” and allowed multiple selections.
Explain why this sector graph is incorrect.

spec.description: Editable graphic preserving63%,70%,60% and original distorted sector angles (approximately112°,145°,103°), source caption and News mark. Percentages intentionally are not normalised.
spec.purposefulShading: Three standard-palette fills distinguish the three response sectors. Decorative background removed; source evidence retained.

answer.short: The percentages total 193%, not 100%. Multiple selections overlap, so a sector graph is unsuitable.
answer.worked:
$63\%+70\%+60\%=193\%$.
A sector graph represents parts of one whole. These responses overlap because voters could make multiple selections, so they cannot form a single 100% whole.
